title: Thorn and Hollow
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, smuggler Mara Delacroix discovers the wards were never meant to keep enemies out—they were keeping something buried beneath the mountains asleep. The dying Guild of the Hollow Road, her only family, is torn between selling the secret to a desperate crown or destroying it forever. Hunted by an exiled war-priest, a traitor within the guild, and the encroaching endless winter, Mara must choose between loyalty to the people who raised her and the truth that could save—or doom—the lowlands. In the end she seals the buried power at the cost of the guild's roads and her own name, forging a new family from survivors who choose to stay.
about_author: B. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six winters mapping passes through real mountain ranges before turning to fiction. They write about borders, weather, and the families people build when institutions fail them.

chapters.title: The Last Clear Night
chapters.summary: Mara guides a contraband shipment through the Thornfell passes under a sky full of stars, establishing her skill, her debts, and her fierce loyalty to the hollowed-out Guild. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: quiet pride on the edge of loss.

chapters.title: Wards Like Old Scars
chapters.summary: At the guildhall, aging guildmaster Oren Vey shows Mara the ancient ward-stones humming along the border—maintenance the guild has secretly performed for centuries. She learns the smuggling routes were cover for something older. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: unsettling revelation beneath familiar ground.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Every ward-stone fails at once; the stars go out like snuffed candles. Avalanches seal the high passes, and something vast shifts beneath the mountain. The guild gathers in panic. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: terror disguised as competence.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Oren reveals the truth: the guild was founded to guard a sealed power beneath Thornfell, and the wards' failure means it is waking. He names Mara, youngest and least compromised, as the one to carry the sealing key south. POV: Oren. Emotional beat: burden passed down like inheritance.

chapters.title: A Traitor's Footprints
chapters.summary: Evidence suggests someone inside the guild sabotaged the wards. Suspicion fractures the found family; old friend Tam Rusk argues for selling the secret to the crown instead of hiding it. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to crack against truth.

chapters.title: Down the Hollow Road
chapters.summary: Mara flees into the deep tunnels with the key, guided by gruff veteran Sefa Ironhale. Below, they find the first signs of the exiled war-priest Cassian Vole already digging toward the buried power. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread and stubborn resolve.

chapters.title: The Priest of Ash
chapters.summary: Cassian captures them briefly, preaching that the buried power belongs to the people the wards displaced generations ago. His conviction unsettles Mara more than his cruelty. They escape, but he lets them go—curious what she'll do. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: doubt planted by an enemy's honesty.

chapters.title: Refuge at Greyford
chapters.summary: In a snowbound valley town, Mara finds refugees fleeing the starless dark and meets Ilse, a sharp-tongued healer who joins them. The town's suffering makes the abstract stakes painfully human. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: compassion hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: Crown Men on the Pass
chapters.summary: Royal soldiers intercept the group, offering protection in exchange for the key. Mara realizes the crown knew about the wards all along and let them decay. A bloody skirmish forces them off the official roads. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: betrayal by every institution she feared.

chapters.title: Tam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam resurfaces, revealed as the saboteur—he opened the wards believing the power could end the famine in the lowlands. He begs Mara to join him. She refuses, but his logic lodges like a splinter. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: sympathetic villainy, love curdled into justification.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: The starless night brings unnatural cold; crops die, rivers freeze mid-current. The party shelters in a ruined watchtower where Sefa confesses she helped bury the power long ago—and what it cost her then. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: grief as instruction.

chapters.title: Voices Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Mara begins dreaming in the buried thing's voice—it speaks through the key, offering her everything she's lost. She wakes holding frost-burned palms and tells no one. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: seduction of despair.

chapters.title: The Guildhall Burns
chapters.summary: Word arrives that soldiers and Cassian's followers razed the guildhall; Oren is dead. The guild Mara loved exists now only in its scattered survivors. She formally breaks from the old order and claims leadership. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Allies of No Law
chapters.summary: Mara rallies smugglers, deserters, and Greyford refugees into an unlikely company—justice outside any law. Ilse and Sefa become her lieutenants; the plan forms to reseal the power from inside the mountain. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: found family forged in open rebellion.

chapters.title: The Frozen Gate
chapters.summary: The company fights through Cassian's besieged camp at the mountain gate. Mara confronts him again; this time she argues back, and some of his followers defect, moved by her honesty about the wards' original sin. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: winning people, not just battles.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Into the deep galleries they go, past murals showing the sealing was never justice—only exile. Tam reappears ahead of them, racing for the heart-chamber. An icefall separates Mara from half her company. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: sacrifice looming with every step down.

chapters.title: The Heart-Chamber
chapters.summary: Mara reaches the buried power—a wounded, ancient presence, neither demon nor god. It offers to end the winter if freed. Tam arrives and, seeing the truth in Mara's memories shared through the key, turns his blade on Cassian instead. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: redemption bought at the point of no return.

chapters.title: Thorn and Hollow
chapters.summary: Climax: Cassian, wounded and fanatical, tries to shatter the seal himself. Mara chooses not destruction but communion—she offers the power acknowledgment instead of imprisonment, using the key to bind it willingly to the mountain rather than cage it. The stars flicker back, changed. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: mercy as the hardest victory.

chapters.title: The Price of the Key
chapters.summary: The binding drains the passes' magic; the smugglers' roads close forever, and Sefa, bound to the old rite, stays behind as living anchor. Mara carries her out as far as the threshold and says goodbye. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: farewell without regret.

chapters.title: Terms With the Crown
chapters.summary: Mara negotiates with the chastened crown from strength: amnesty for the company, aid for Greyford, and the guild's true history written into law. Justice outside the law becomes reform within it—on her terms. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: power wielded gently.

chapters.title: What We Bury Together
chapters.summary: Spring's false dawn returns. The survivors rebuild—not the guild, but something new and unhidden. Tam, pardoned but not forgiven, plants ward-stone seeds along the old roads. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: forgiveness as ongoing work, not gift.

chapters.title: First Star Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: One year later, Mara leads a small company up a reopened pass under a single returned star. She carries the key still, now a covenant rather than a burden, surrounded by the family that chose to stay. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: earned peace, watchful hope.
